Task: Write a quick note explaining why TCP differs from UDP.

TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) and UDP (User Datagram Protocol) differ primarily in reliability and connection behavior. TCP is connection-oriented, establishing a connection via a three-way handshake before data transfer, and guarantees delivery through acknowledgments, retransmissions, and ordered packet assembly. It also handles flow and congestion control. UDP, by contrast, is connectionless and "fire-and-forget"—it sends datagrams without confirming receipt, ordering, or error recovery. This makes UDP faster and lighter, ideal for real-time applications like video streaming, gaming, and DNS lookups where speed matters more than perfect reliability. TCP is preferred for file transfers, web browsing, and email where data integrity is critical.
